messages.author: 61ddffa51c481ed7
messages.subject: region.N function for multi-session models
parts:
Hello, 

It is me again (sorry).
I have been trying to use region.N to get an estimated number of individuals. I am using multi-session models (six sessions: A, B, C, D, E and F):

The R help file says:
pooled.RN = TRUE handles the special case of a multi-session model in which the region of interest spans several patches (i.e., sampling in each session is localised within region. This is not yet fully implemented

1) I am wondering what "not yet fully implemented" means?

I have therefore tried:
> region.N(m36, pooled.RN=TRUE)
Error in apply(region, 2, range) : dim(X) must have a positive length

> region.N(m36, pooled.RN=TRUE, session = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"))
Error in apply(region, 2, range) : dim(X) must have a positive length

> region.N(m35, pooled.RN=TRUE, region = list(ruggAcovmask, ruggBcovmask, ruggCcovmask, ruggDcovmask, ruggEcovmask, ruggFcovmask), session = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"))
Error in apply(region, 2, range) : dim(X) must have a positive length

So then, I tried to do it one session at a time, which seemed to work for the expected N (E.N) but I am not sure what is going on with the realised N (R.N) estimates:

> region.N(m35, region = ruggAcovmask, session = "A")
    estimate SE.estimate      lcl      ucl n
E.N 15.25614    2.970633 10.45299 22.26633 6
R.N 14.80720         NaN      NaN      NaN 6

> region.N(m35, region = ruggBcovmask, session = "B")
        estimate SE.estimate      lcl      ucl n
E.N     10.34183    2.260648 6.771702 15.79417 5
R.N -40967.74010         NaN      NaN      NaN 5

> region.N(m35, region = ruggCcovmask, session = "C")
         estimate SE.estimate      lcl      ucl n
E.N      9.649189    1.936364 6.536692 14.24373 4
R.N -28747.504851         NaN      NaN      NaN 4

> region.N(m35, region = ruggDcovmask, session = "D")
       estimate SE.estimate      lcl      ucl n
E.N     10.6913    2.344553 6.991231 16.34962 7
R.N -10504.2139         NaN      NaN      NaN 7

> region.N(m35, region = ruggEcovmask, session = "E")
        estimate SE.estimate      lcl      ucl  n
E.N     14.61521    2.983026 9.836507 21.71547 10
R.N -25689.69669         NaN      NaN      NaN 10

> region.N(m35, region = ruggFcovmask, session = "F")
        estimate SE.estimate      lcl      ucl  n
E.N     16.70956    3.532603 11.09109 25.17421 10
R.N -61180.81882         NaN      NaN      NaN 10

2) Do these NaN and abnormal R.N estimates have to do with the fact that region.N is not fully implemented for multi-session models?
Is it still possible for me to use the session-specific E.N estimates?

Let me know, thanks very much
Kind regards, 

Elsa

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: region.N function for multi-session models
parts:
1. I can't recall, but I see this line in the code that suggests it doesn't handle session-specific models
 if (pooled.RN)
        ## use only model for first session
        session <- session[1]
2. The E.N should be OK, and you can check the estimates just by multiplying (predicted) density by area. Nonsense R.N are easy to generate and I can't say where yours are coming from: would need to investigate the relationships among sessions, regions and habitat mask(s).

Murray
